source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Heart failure generally following a fairly predictable, linear disease course that leaves fairly little need for advance planning","B":"Heart failure often has an unpredictable trajectory with risk of sudden decompensation, making proactive advance care planning valuable","C":"This kind of conversation generally being avoided out of concern that it may cause the client unnecessary distress","D":"Advance care planning being considered relevant mainly to cancer diagnoses, rather than to chronic conditions like heart failure"}}
source_row.rationale: Advance care planning is important in heart failure because this condition often has an unpredictable trajectory, with risk of sudden decompensation or death, making proactive conversations about values and preferences valuable earlier in the disease course rather than only during a crisis.
source_row.source_detail: Rationale for Proactive Advance Care Planning in HF
source_row.source_name: AHA — Advance Care Planning in Heart Failure
